newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Valeo hunt for French buyer stumbles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Valeo hunt for French buyer stumbles.

text.p: Long efforts to find a French buyer for car parts supplier Valeo hit a roadblock on Tuesday when the latest candidate, industrial company CGIP, denied reports it would launch a takeover bid.
CGIP said it was not preparing a public offer for Valeo or Cerus, Italian industrialist Carlo De Benedetti's French holding company, which controls Valeo through a 28 percent stake.

"We don't deny that we have contacts and discussions but we do deny any plans for a public offer," a CGIP spokeswoman said. The two companies were discussing their options, she said, but would not elaborate.
The statement took the steam out of a rally in Cerus and Valeo shares that followed a newspaper report outlining what it said was a detailed three-part plan by CGIP to acquire Cerus.
French carmakers, pressing the government to help ensure French ownership of their leading supplier, applauded the plan.
Valeo, Cerus's plum asset, became a takeover target in February when De Benedetti commissioned bankers to study possible asset sales to help him shore up his business empire.
He resigned as chairman of Italian mobile phone and PC group Olivetti last week.

Among the companies reported to be interested in Valeo were American giants General Motors and TRW, which would probably be willing to pay a hefty 20 billion francs ($3.90 billion) or more order to expand in Europe.
But French carmakers, notably PSA Peugeot Citroen's outspoken chairman Jacques Calvet, said they would not stand for a U.S. buyout.
Industry sources say GM backed off but an outsider might yet launch a last-minute counterbid.

"This story isn't finished. There's a possibility that a better offer may emerge," said one Paris analyst. "But then this is France, and with everyone clamouring for a French solution, there wasn't going to be a wide open competition for Valeo."
Some analysts said the key problem with an exclusively French solution was that it would probably rob De Benedetti and Cerus and Valeo shareholders of the best offer on the market.

Buyout terms published by the newspaper Les Echos on Tuesday, and CGIP's subsequent denial, wrought havoc on the Paris bourse. Selling in Cerus and Valeo shares was so heavy that both stocks were briefly suspended.
Many traders were furious. "Don't they read the papers at CGIP? They waited until midday to deny this report? Look at these trading volumes," one said.
Shares in Cerus finished down 2.80 francs at 133 after see-sawing between 128.30 and 153.50 francs. Valeo's stock rose 9.10 francs to 279.60 after a similar rollercoaster ride.
Analysts were puzzled by CGIP's talk of options, with some reckoning a deal could still be in the offing.
Others speculated the press leak may have torpedoed a deal, or that French bourse authorities may be insisting on an offer that does not appear to be bypassing Valeo's other shareholders.
Under bourse rules, CGIP would not have to launch a takeover bid for Valeo if it bought only Cerus's 28 percent stake.
"CGIP is still interested but they're probably feeling wary now," a French industry source said. He said the leaks looked like a veiled invitation for a counter-offer.
Valeo declined comment on the reports and Cerus officials were unavailable for comment.
Electronics group Sagem, reported by Les Echos as planning to take a stake in the new merged company, denied that it had struck any such deal. ($1=5.129 French Franc)
